passage:
A museum displayed a tiny piece of moon rock. It was smaller than a coin, kept inside thick glass.
Some visitors were disappointed. They expected something larger and more beautiful. The guide said the rock mattered not because of its size, but because of where it had been.
A student looked at the gray stone and imagined the long journey from Earth to the Moon and back. Suddenly, the small rock felt heavier than it looked.
The guide added that science often changes how people value objects. A stone from a road may be ignored. A stone from another world can make people look up.
